classification.difficultyReason: Construct a grouped frequency table and interpret class boundaries for measurements recorded to the nearest millimetre.

inlines.text: The following set of raw data shows the lengths, recorded to the nearest millimetre, of 40 leaves taken from a particular tree.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct a frequency table with classes 25–29, 30–34 and so on.

inlines.text: Count each recorded length in its class.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In which class is a leaf measured as 29.7 mm included?

answer.worked: 29.7 mm rounds to 30 mm to the nearest millimetre, so it belongs to the 30–34 mm class. The class boundaries are 29.5 mm and 34.5 mm.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In which class is a leaf measured as 34.3 mm included?

answer.worked: 34.3 mm rounds to 34 mm to the nearest millimetre, so it belongs to the 30–34 mm class. The class boundaries are 29.5 mm and 34.5 mm.
